candidate.answerReason: The conditioning interval has length 25, and the favorable part has length 241/100. Their ratio is 241/2500, matching B.

methods.label: Compare interval lengths
methods.explanation:
Work with intervals for \(x\), because \(x\) is the quantity chosen uniformly. The given condition means
\[
12\le\sqrt{x}<13,
\]
so, squaring these nonnegative quantities,
\[
144\le x<169.
\]
This entire interval lies between \(100\) and \(200\). After conditioning, \(x\) is uniform on this interval of length \(169-144=25\).

The requested event is equivalent to
\[
120\le\sqrt{100x}<121,
\]
which gives
\[
14400\le100x<14641,
\qquad
144\le x<\frac{14641}{100}.
\]
This favorable interval is contained in the conditioning interval, and its length is
\[
\frac{14641}{100}-144=\frac{241}{100}.
\]
For a uniform choice, probability is the favorable length divided by the total available length. Thus the conditional probability is
\[
\frac{241/100}{25}=\boxed{\frac{241}{2500}},
\]
choice B. Including or excluding individual endpoints does not change a uniform interval probability.
